title: Introductory programming coursework with guardrailed CodeHelp
summary: Students complete quizzes, assignments, and reading responses in an introductory computer and data science course. They may use CodeHelp for immediate programming support; the LLM assistant explains and guides but is designed not to output solution code.

sources.title: Patterns of Student Help-Seeking When Using a Large Language Model-Powered Programming Assistant
sources.evidence_quote: Students were encouraged to use CodeHelp for assistance first before asking the instructor or TA

assessment.summary: Complete semester-long introductory Python coursework with optional on-demand help.
student_actions: Submit code, errors, and questions to CodeHelp when stuck.
Apply conceptual or debugging guidance without receiving direct solution code.

outputs.artifact: Course assignments, quizzes, and reading responses

student_role.description: CodeHelp was optional but recommended before human help and used guardrails to suppress generated solution code.

grading.method: Course points came from quizzes, assignments, and reading responses.

provenance.extraction_method: Full PDF read from pdftotext output.

reported_results: 49 of 52 students submitted 2,591 queries over 12 weeks; tool usage correlated modestly with course performance.

evidence_excerpts.quote: Students were encouraged to use CodeHelp for assistance first before asking the instructor or TA
